record.title: Chen–Lev conjecture on periodic intersections of representation-equivalent sets
record.statement:
Let $C$ and $D$ be different sets of nonnegative integers, and let $R_C(n)$ count representations of $n$ as a sum of two distinct elements of $C$, with the analogous definition for $D$. Assume

$$
C\cup D=\mathbb N,
$$

$$
C\cap D=r+m\mathbb N,
$$

where $r\ge0$ and $m\ge2$ are integers.

**Chen–Lev conjecture.** If $R_C(n)=R_D(n)$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists an integer $l\ge1$ such that

$$
r=2^{2l}-1,\qquad m=2^{2l+1}-1.
$$

This question seeks a classification of covering pairs with periodic intersection and identical two-element representation functions. The source presents the assertion as a question posed by Chen and Lev; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Sándor Z. Kiss and Csaba Sándor, “On the structure of sets which have coinciding representation functions”, arXiv:1702.04499 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.04499

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: Rainbow forest packing conjecture for globally bounded graphs
record.statement: Let $\varepsilon>0$. A graph is **globally $m$-bounded** if no colour is used on more than $m$ edges, and a forest of order $k$ has $k$ edges. **Rainbow forest packing conjecture.** There exists an $m\in\mathbb{N}$, depending on $\varepsilon$, such that for every $k$, every properly coloured, globally $m$-bounded graph $G$ with $km$ edges has at least $(1-\varepsilon)m$ edge-disjoint rainbow forests of order $k$. This is posed as a question in the concluding remarks and no resolution is supplied, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Richard Montgomery, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Decompositions into spanning rainbow structures”, arXiv:1805.07564 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07564

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: Open problem on realizing every chromatic number by interval distance graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_D$ be the distance graph on the plane whose vertices are the points of $\mathbb{R}^2$, with two points adjacent when their distance lies in $D$. For $b>1$, write $G_{[1,b]}$ for the graph with distance set $[1,b]$, and let $\chi$ denote chromatic number.

**Realization problem.** For any integer $k\ge 7$, there exists $b>1$ such that

$$
\chi(G_{[1,b]})=k.
$$

The problem asks whether interval distance graphs can realize every chromatic number at least $7$. The paper notes that several values, including $8$, $10$, and $11$, are not currently determined by the available constructions, so the question remains open.
record.source_name: Joanna Chybowska-Sokół, Konstanty Junosza-Szaniawski and Krzysztof Węsek, “Coloring distance graphs on the plane”, arXiv:2201.04499 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04499

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2022). “We post as an open question if there is a solid 8-coloring of $G_{[1,b]}$ for any $b>\sqrt{7}/2$.”

record.title: The distant 2-colored components extension conjecture for planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph and let $W\subseteq V(G)$ be such that $G[W]$ is bipartite, with any two components of $G[W]$ at distance at least $100$ from each other. A coloring of $G[W]$ is **2-colored** when each component of $G[W]$ receives at most two colors. **Distant 2-colored components extension conjecture.** Any coloring of $G[W]$ such that each component is 2-colored should extend to a $5$-coloring of $G$. The cited theorem gives a positive answer to a list-coloring version of this conjecture for ordinary colorings, with a different distance constant; the conjecture itself is presented as a question in the source.
record.source_name: Joshua Nevin, “Distant 2-Colored Components on Embeddings Part I: Connecting Faces”, arXiv:2207.12531 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12531

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).

record.title: Bounded-dimensional support conjecture for minimal slice-rank decompositions
record.statement:
Let $d \ge 3$ and $k \ge 1$ be integers. An order-$d$ tensor $T$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ has slice rank $k$ if it can be expressed using $k$ slices, where each slice has the form of a function in one variable multiplied by a function in the remaining $d-1$ variables. For each mode, write $[n_j]=\{1,\dots,n_j\}$, and let $\overline{x_j}$ denote the tuple of variables other than $x_j$.

**Bounded-dimensional support conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $C(d,k)$ such that, for every order-$d$ tensor $T$ over an arbitrary field $\mathbb{F}$ with slice rank $k$, there are linear subspaces

$$
A_1 \subset \mathbb{F}^{n_1},\dots,A_d \subset \mathbb{F}^{n_d}
$$

with dimension at most $C(d,k)$ such that the following holds: whenever $r_1,\dots,r_d$ are nonnegative integers satisfying

$$
\nr_1+\dots+r_d=k,
$$

and functions $a_{j,i}:[n_j]\to\mathbb{F}$, for $j\in[d]$ and $i\in[r_j]$, together with functions $b_{j,i}:\prod_{j'\ne j}[n_{j'}]\to\mathbb{F}$, satisfy

$$
T(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\sum_{j=1}^d\sum_{i=1}^{r_j}a_{j,i}(x_j)b_{j,i}(\overline{x_j}),
$$

then

$$
\langle a_{1,1},\dots,a_{1,r_1}\rangle\subset A_1,\dots,\langle a_{d,1},\dots,a_{d,r_d}\rangle\subset A_d.
$$

This would give a field-uniform bound on the subspaces supporting the one-variable factors in every minimal-length slice-rank decomposition. The question arises because the paper's preceding results do not provide such a uniform statement: over infinite fields the analogous theorem fails, while over finite fields the available bounds depend on the field and can grow square-exponentially in the slice rank. The source presents this as an open question rather than reporting a resolution.
record.source_name: Thomas Karam, “Small sunflowers and the structure of slice rank decompositions”, arXiv:2308.07101 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Minimum-size conjecture for 3-connected graphs with cyclic neighborhoods
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and size $m$. Assume that $G$ is **3-connected** and that every neighborhood of a vertex contains a cycle. **Minimum-size conjecture.** Then

$$
m\geq \frac{7}{3}(n-1).
$$

The question concerns graphs with no forest cut: such graphs are necessarily 3-connected and have a cycle in every vertex neighborhood. The family $G_k$ described in the paper has $3k+4$ vertices and $7k+7$ edges and satisfies these structural conditions, motivating the proposed lower bound; whether any such graph can have fewer edges remains open.
record.source_name: Vsevolod Chernyshev, Johannes Rauch and Dieter Rautenbach, “Forest Cuts in Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2409.17724 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17724

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

record.title: Tower-bound problem for induced Ramsey numbers of cliques
record.statement:
For graphs $G$ and $F$, let $G\mathrel{\overset{\makebox[0pt]{\text{\normalfont\tiny\sffamily ind}}}{\rightarrow}} (F)^{K_r}$ mean that every $2$-coloring of the complete subgraphs of $G$ on $r$ vertices yields an induced copy of $F$ whose complete subgraphs of size $r$ are all the same color. Let $R_{\operatorname{ind}}^{K_r}(F)$ be the smallest number of vertices of a graph $G$ satisfying this property. Define the tower function by $t_0(x)=x$ and $t_i(x)=2^{t_{i-1}(x)}$. **Tower-bound problem.** Show that for any graph $F$ on $n$ vertices, there is a constant $c=c(r)$ depending only on $r$ such that

$$
R_{\operatorname{ind}}^{K_r}(F)\leq t_{r-1}(cn).
$$

The authors note that their arguments extend to $r\geq 3$, while the displayed problem seeks bounds matching the growth of the classical Ramsey numbers $R^{(r)}(F)$. The source does not report a resolution.

record.title: Puncturing-inclusion conjecture for MRD codes
record.statement: Let $n,d\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $1<d<n$, and let $\mathbb F$ be a finite field. An **MRD code** is a maximum rank-distance code. **Puncturing-inclusion conjecture.** There exists an $[n\times(n-1),n(n-d),d]_{\mathbb F}$ MRD code $\mathcal C$ such that its puncturing on one row is contained in an $[(n-1)\times(n-1),(n-1)(n-d+1),d-1]_{\mathbb F}$ MRD code. This open problem is equivalent to a smaller instance of the Etzion–Silberstein conjecture.
record.source_name: Hugo Beeloo-Sauerbier Couvée and Alessandro Neri, “Irreducible Ferrers diagrams in the Etzion-Silberstein conjecture”, arXiv:2604.27868 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27868

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2026). “While the conjecture has been established for several classes of diagrams (including rectangular, monotone, and MDS-constructible cases), it remains open in general.”

record.title: The extremal graph classification conjecture for perfect edge dominating sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an extremal graph on $n\geq 6$ vertices among all graphs on $n$ vertices, where extremal means that $G$ maximizes the number of perfect edge dominating sets. Let $C_k$ denote the cycle on $k$ vertices, let $aC_k$ denote the disjoint union of $a$ copies of $C_k$, and define

$$
\mathcal G=\left\{\frac{n}{3}C_3:n\geq 6\text{ and }n\equiv 0\pmod 3\right\}\cup
$$

$$
\left\{\frac{n-4}{3}C_3+C_4:n\geq 7\text{ and }n\equiv 1\pmod 3\right\}\cup
$$

$$
\left\{\frac{n-8}{3}C_3+2C_4:n\geq 8\text{ and }n\equiv 2\pmod 3\right\}.
$$

**Extremal graph classification conjecture.** Every such extremal graph satisfies

$$
G\in\mathcal G.
$$

This open problem proposes a complete classification of the graphs maximizing the number of perfect edge dominating sets among all graphs of order $n$. The preceding results determine extremal graphs in several restricted graph classes, but the unrestricted classification remains open.
record.source_name: Luciano N. Grippo, Min Chih Lin, Verónica Moyano and Camilo Vera, “Counting perfect edge dominating sets: extremal results and linear-time algorithms”, arXiv:2607.03894 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03894

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2026). “We conclude with the following open problem.”

record.title: Existence of a λ-harmonic function satisfying a spectral inequality
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ be a bounded open set with a sufficiently smooth boundary. Let $(\lambda_j,u_j)$ be the Dirichlet-Laplacian eigenvalues and corresponding orthonormal eigenfunctions in $L^2(\Omega)$, with eigenvalues ordered non-decreasingly and repeated according to multiplicity. For $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, define
\[
H(\lambda)=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):\Delta v+\lambda v=0\text{ in }\Omega\}.
\]
Is it true that, for every $\lambda>\lambda_1$, there exists a $\lambda$-harmonic function $g\in H(\lambda)$ such that
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda_j-\lambda}{\lambda_j}\,\bigl|\langle g,u_j\rangle\bigr|^2<0?
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12005), page 52. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Brändén’s hyperbolic-polynomial partition theorem
record.statement: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer and let $\varepsilon>0$. Suppose $h$ is hyperbolic with respect to $e\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m\in\Lambda^+(e)$ satisfy $\operatorname{rk}(u_i)\le 1$, $\operatorname{tr}(u_i)\le\varepsilon$ for $1\le i\le m$, and $u_1+\cdots+u_m=e$. Then there is a partition $S_1\cup\cdots\cup S_k=[m]$ such that, for every $j\in[k]$, $\lambda_{\max}\!\left(\sum_{i\in S_j}u_i\right)\le \frac{1}{k}\,\delta(k\varepsilon,m)$, where $\delta(\alpha,m):=\left(1-\frac1m+\sqrt{\alpha+\frac1m\left(1-\frac1m\right)}\right)^2$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13674), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Discrepancy of high-dimensional permutations
record.statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. A $d$-dimensional permutation is a $0$–$1$ array $A$ indexed by $[n]^{d+1}$ such that, for every $1\le i\le d+1$ and every choice of $\alpha_j\in[n]$ for $j\ne i$, there is exactly one $x\in[n]$ with $A(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{i-1},x,\alpha_{i+1},\ldots,\alpha_{d+1})=1$. For every $d\ge2$, do there exist arbitrarily large $d$-dimensional permutations $A$ such that, for every box $T=T_1\times\cdots\times T_{d+1}\subseteq[n]^{d+1}$, with $\operatorname{vol}(T):=\prod_{i=1}^{d+1}|T_i|$ and $A(T):=|\{\alpha\in T:A(\alpha)=1\}|$, one has $\left|A(T)-\frac{\operatorname{vol}(T)}{n}\right|=O\!\left(\sqrt{\operatorname{vol}(T)}\right)$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14604), page 8. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Structure of graphs minimizing triangular edges
record.statement: For integers $n\ge 3$ and $n^2/4<e\le\binom{n}{2}$, let $\operatorname{Tr}(G)$ be the number of edges of $G$ contained in triangles, and let $\operatorname{Tr}(n,e)=\min\{\operatorname{Tr}(G):|V(G)|=n,\ |E(G)|=e\}$. Define $\operatorname{Tr}(a,b,c)$ as the class of graphs with a partition $V=A\cup B\cup C$, where $|A|=a$, $|B|=b$, $|C|=c$, $a\ge2$, $B$ and $C$ are independent, $B\cup C$ induces $K_{b,c}$, vertices of $C$ have neighbors only in $B$, and $G[A]$ together with $G[A,B]$ spans more than $\binom{|A|-1}{2}+|A||B|$ edges. Let $\operatorname{Tr}(n,e)$ also denote the subclass of such graphs with $n$ vertices and $e$ edges having the minimum number of triangular edges among these types. If $G$ is an $n$-vertex graph with $e$ edges and $\operatorname{Tr}(G)=\operatorname{Tr}(n,e)$, then $G\in\operatorname{Tr}(n,e)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14604), page 36. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Quantization of spectral curves and DQ-modules
record.statement: Let $\Sigma$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g\ge 2$, let $(E,\phi)$ be a Higgs bundle of rank $r\ge 2$ on $\Sigma$, and let $\widehat{\mathcal W}_{T^*\Sigma}(0)$ be the canonical quantization of $T^*\Sigma$. If $\pi:T^*\Sigma\to\Sigma$ is the canonical projection and $\eta$ is the Liouville form, with spectral curve $S$ given by $S=\{\det(\pi^*\phi-\eta\,\mathrm{id})=0\}$, then there exists a holonomic $\widehat{\mathcal W}_{T^*\Sigma}(0)$-module $\mathcal M$ supported by $S$. Moreover, if $S$ is smooth, then $\mathcal M$ is simple along $S$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/9](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14217), page 46. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Theorem 3: Local uniqueness for $(\gamma,\sigma,\mu)$ in two-photon photoacoustic tomography
record.statement:
In dimension $d=3$, assuming the Grüneisen coefficient $\Gamma$ is known and the background coefficients are sufficiently smooth, there exists a set of $J\ge d+1$ boundary illuminations $\{g_j\}_{j=1}^J$ such that the corresponding linearized internal-data sets $\{\delta H_j\}_{j=1}^J$ and $\{\widetilde{\delta H}_j\}_{j=1}^J$, generated by perturbations $(\delta\gamma,\delta\sigma,\delta\mu)$ and $(\widetilde{\delta\gamma},\widetilde{\delta\sigma},\widetilde{\delta\mu})$, respectively, satisfy
\[
\{\delta H_j\}_{j=1}^J=\{\widetilde{\delta H}_j\}_{j=1}^J
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(\delta\gamma,\delta\sigma,\delta\mu)=(\widetilde{\delta\gamma},\widetilde{\delta\sigma},\widetilde{\delta\mu}),
\]
provided that $\delta\gamma|_{\partial\Omega}=\widetilde{\delta\gamma}|_{\partial\Omega}$. The linearized system is
\[
-\nabla\!\cdot(\delta\gamma\nabla u_j)-\nabla\!\cdot(\gamma\nabla\delta u_j)=-\frac{\delta H_j}{\Gamma},
\qquad
u_j\delta\sigma+|u_j|u_j\delta\mu+(\sigma+2\mu|u_j|)\delta u_j=\frac{\delta H_j}{\Gamma}
\quad\text{in }\Omega,
\]
with the appropriate boundary conditions.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/24](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15432), page 79. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Realizability of cone-preserving graphs
record.statement: For fixed positive integers $m,n$ with $m\ge n$, characterize the directed graphs on $m$ vertices that are realizable as $D_K(A)$ for a proper polyhedral cone $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $m$ extreme rays and a $K$-nonnegative matrix $A$. Here the vertices of $D_K(A)$ are the extreme rays of $K$, and, for extreme rays $R_1=\{\alpha x:\alpha\ge0\}$ and $R_2=\{\alpha y:\alpha\ge0\}$ with nonzero $x,y\in K$, there is an edge $R_1\to R_2$ exactly when $y$ belongs to the face of $K$ generated by $Ax$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/52](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15957), page 32. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Subgraphs of large connectivity and chromatic number
record.statement: For each $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ with chromatic number at least $7k+1$ contains a subgraph $H$ with both connectivity and chromatic number at least $k$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/9790352), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Girth-preserving version for induced subgraphs of large chromatic number
record.statement: **Conjecture 4.** For every graph $F$ with at least one cycle, there exists a constant $b_F$ and graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large chromatic number and the same girth as $F$ such that every $F$-free induced subgraph of $G$ is $b_F$-colourable.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2022/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/10252930), page 48. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Existence of subspace Steiner designs
record.statement:
For every prime power $q$ and integers $s>r\ge 1$, there is a threshold $n_2(q,s)$ such that, whenever $n\ge n_2(q,s)$ and
$$
\begin{bmatrix}s-i\\ r-i\end{bmatrix}_q\ \middle|\ \begin{bmatrix}n-i\\ r-i\end{bmatrix}_q
$$
for every $0\le i\le r-1$, there exists an $(n,s,r)_q$-design: a multicollection of $s$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ in which every $r$-dimensional subspace is contained in exactly one member.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2023/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12697684), page 69. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Unavoidability of shuffles in permutations
record.statement: A permutation \[?] of size \(pk\) is a \(k\)-shuffle if it can be partitioned into \(k\) subsequences such that every subsequence is an occurrence of the same pattern of length \(p\). Conjecture: For each \(k\), there exists a constant \(n_0(k)\) such that every permutation of size \(n>n_0(k)\) contains a factor (consecutive subsequence) of length at least \(2k\) that is a \(k\)-shuffle.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2024/6](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14298158), page 15. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
